must: **Waterfall**: strict order, no going back, used with **stage/quality gates**.
**V-Model**: left = specification/design, right = integration/testing, paired levels; safety-critical (IEC 61508-3).
**Component/matrix (RUP)**: processes × phases; processes run across the whole project.
Prototyping: **exploratory** (find requirements) vs **experimental** (validate solution); **evolutionary** (becomes product) vs **throw-away**; **rapid** = throw-away.
Iterative/incremental: **reduce risk through fast feedback**; iteration = refine, increment = add.
**Spiral (Boehm)**: first explicit iterative model, **risk analysis every loop**. **Release trains**: fixed dates, time-box.
Methodology-driven: structured (SSADM, SADT, Yourdon), **formal methods**, **Cleanroom**, **design thinking**.
traps: Slide 13's 'Incremental' definition is actually the **waterfall** definition.
Exploratory vs evolutionary are **different dimensions** (purpose vs fate).
likely: Recommend a life cycle model for a scenario and justify.
Explain the spiral model's emphasis on risk.
tricks: Time-box (release train) = **fix the date, flex the scope**; waterfall = fix scope, date slips.

story.problem: Every project needs an overall shape: when to specify, build and test.
story.fix: Life cycle models: waterfall, V-Model, RUP, prototyping, iterative, spiral and release trains.
story.next: Plan-driven models struggle when requirements keep changing.

terms.def: Phases in strict order with little or no iteration.
A formal check before the next phase may start.
Waterfall bent into a V pairing each spec level with a test level.
Rational Unified Process: processes × phases matrix model.
Refined repeatedly until it becomes the product.
Boehm's iterative model with risk analysis each loop.
Fixed date; scope flexes to fit.
